summary: Family fastener distributor (139 M EUR); we are only 0.03 % of turnover. Holds 30-50 % of the M12 bolt, nut and washer; 70650 and 70630 are active second sources. Historically asks ~2.5 % and settles ~0 (kept 5 %). Second shift idle since spring, so it wants work: the one-supplier fastener kit (P07) and a binding volume move it. Arena: never walked, gave 2.4-5.2 % from its opening (median ~4.4 %) by round 3-4.
notes: Needs volume to refill its idle second shift; the kit may go to one supplier only. KAM says moves above 2 % need its pricing committee, yet in arena it moved up to ~5 % within 4 rounds. Quality and index arguments did not move it in arena. OTD 88.6 % vs 95 % target, 71 complaints in 3 years.
fears: losing kit volume to another supplier

evidence.quote: price changes above 2 % need the approval of their pricing committee, which meets every two weeks
they could take additional parts at short notice; the second shift has been on hold since spring
A binding higher volume would help us and can improve the price.

arguments: binding volume commitment with volume schedule CSV
avoid: index or cost-driver arguments (no change in arena)
changing any term after its final offer
tactics: Open deep and frame the deal as the whole fastener kit (bolts, nuts, washers) for 36 months.
State a binding annual volume early and attach the volume schedule; it asks 'Which volume can you commit to?' and moves on it.
Treat payment days as a priced trade: compare its Zahlungsziel alternatives at ~7-8 %/yr.
Make one visible move per round; expect its final offer around round 4 and accept it unchanged.
If a step above 2 % stalls, point to the added kit volume as the reason for its pricing committee.
playbook.expected_concession: First counter only ~2.6 % below its opening, then small steps; ended 2.4-5.2 % below opening, final offer mostly in round 4 (P07: 5.74 to 5.44-5.60).
